stem: What is a record producer in Service Catalog?

rationale: A record producer is a catalog item with a friendly form that creates a task-based record — like an incident — instead of going through a regular task form. Same catalog look and feel, different output.

distractor_notes.C: A list of requested items is a report or list view.
distractor_notes.D: Identification rules are CMDB / Data Foundations configuration.

stem: Which statements about record producers are correct?

options.text: They generate a task-based record (for example, an incident) rather than a requested item

rationale: Record producers look like catalog items but output a task record such as an incident, and they should be reserved for task-based records. To create requested items the right way — so workflows fire as expected — use catalog items, not record producers.

distractor_notes.D: Requested items should be created from catalog items, not record producers.
distractor_notes.E: Checkout style is unrelated to record producers; they submit directly.

stem: A manager needs to order equipment for a brand-new employee who does not yet have an account in the system. What catalog capability supports this?

options.text: Requesting items on behalf of another user (the 'requested for' capability, governed by glide.sc.req_for.roles)

rationale: Ordering for someone else is exactly the 'requested for' / order-on-behalf capability, controlled by glide.sc.req_for.roles — so a manager can request items for a new hire.

distractor_notes.B: Cascading copies variable values within an order guide; it isn't about ordering for another user.
distractor_notes.C: A record producer creates a task record, not an order on someone's behalf.
distractor_notes.D: A known error article documents a problem's cause and workaround.

stem: You are building a new catalog item in Catalog Builder and want to define its fulfillment as a series of modern, flow-based steps rather than a legacy workflow. What should you configure?
rationale: A step-based service fulfillment flow lets you define the fulfillment steps directly in Catalog Builder — the modern, flow-based path instead of an execution plan or legacy workflow.

distractor_notes.B: User criteria control visibility/access, not fulfillment steps.
distractor_notes.C: Dynamic categories organize items for browsing.
distractor_notes.D: A variable set is reusable fields, not a fulfillment definition.

references.title: Configure a step-based service fulfillment flow

stem: A request lands with the wrong team and actually needs to be handled by Facilities instead of IT. What is the appropriate action?

options.text: Transfer the request to the other department, with or without resolution, so the right team can fulfill it
Delete the request and tell the user to resubmit
Convert the request into a problem
Close it as resolved without action

rationale: Transferring the request to the correct department routes it to the team that can fulfill it while preserving the record and history — far better than deleting or closing it.

distractor_notes.B: Deleting and resubmitting loses history and frustrates the user.
distractor_notes.C: A misrouted request isn't a problem record.
distractor_notes.D: Closing without action leaves the user's need unmet.

references.title: Transfer a request to another department
